grade_calibration.notes: Levels 1-4 correspond to standard grade 5 curriculum. Levels 5-7 are advanced/enrichment. Levels 8-10 are olympiad-style (multi-step, requires insight, not just procedure).

subtopics.name: Equivalence & Simplification
subtopics.description: Recognizing equivalent fractions, reducing to lowest terms, converting between improper fractions and mixed numbers.

lesson.summary: Two fractions are equivalent when they represent the same amount, even though the numbers look different.
lesson.example_text: 1/2 of a pizza is the same amount as 2/4 of the same pizza — just cut into more, smaller slices.

subtopics.fallback_hint: Try drawing two bars the same size. Split one into more, smaller pieces — does the shaded amount change?

subtopics.name: Comparing & Ordering
subtopics.description: Comparing fractions with unlike denominators, ordering sets of fractions, placing fractions between two given fractions.

lesson.summary: To compare fractions with different denominators, it helps to picture how much of the whole each one covers.
lesson.example_text: 2/3 covers more of the bar than 3/5 does, even though 5 is a bigger number than 3.

subtopics.fallback_hint: Draw both fractions as bars of the same length. Which one has more shaded in?

subtopics.name: Addition
subtopics.description: Adding fractions: like denominators, unlike denominators, mixed numbers, more than two terms.

lesson.summary: Adding fractions with the same denominator just means adding up the shaded pieces — the denominator stays the same.
lesson.example_text: 1/4 of a bar plus 2/4 more of the same bar covers 3/4 in total.

subtopics.fallback_hint: If the denominators match, you only need to add the numerators — the denominator stays the same.

subtopics.name: Subtraction
subtopics.description: Subtracting fractions: like denominators, unlike denominators, mixed numbers with regrouping (borrowing).

lesson.summary: Subtracting fractions with the same denominator means taking away shaded pieces from what you started with.
lesson.example_text: Start with 3/4 shaded, take away 1/4, and 2/4 is left.

subtopics.fallback_hint: If the denominators match, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same.

subtopics.name: Multiplication
subtopics.description: Fraction x whole number, fraction x fraction, mixed numbers, cancelling before multiplying, 'of' as multiplication.

lesson.summary: Multiplying two fractions is like finding the overlap when you shade rows for one fraction and columns for the other.
lesson.example_text: 2/3 of the rows and 3/4 of the columns overlap in 6 of the 12 total squares — so 2/3 x 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.

subtopics.fallback_hint: Multiplying fractions means multiplying straight across: numerator times numerator, denominator times denominator.

subtopics.name: Division
subtopics.description: Dividing by a fraction (reciprocal method), whole / fraction, fraction / fraction, mixed numbers, interpreting division word contexts.

lesson.summary: Dividing by a fraction asks: how many of that fraction's pieces fit inside the amount you have?
lesson.example_text: 3/4 divided by 1/4 asks how many 1/4-size pieces fit inside 3/4 — the answer is 3.

subtopics.fallback_hint: Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal — flip the second fraction, then multiply.

subtopics.name: Word Problems
subtopics.description: Multi-step real-world problems combining operations. Includes part-of-a-part, remaining-quantity, and rate-style problems.

lesson.summary: Word problems combine the fraction skills you already know — the trick is figuring out whether a fraction applies to the whole amount or just to what's left over.
lesson.example_text: "Sara ate 1/2 of a cake, then ate 1/3 of what was left." The 1/3 applies to the remaining half, not the whole cake — so she ate 1/2 + (1/3 of 1/2) = 1/2 + 1/6 = 2/3 of the cake in total.

subtopics.fallback_hint: Read the problem one sentence at a time. Does each fraction apply to the whole amount, or to what is left over?

subtopics.name: Equations with Variables
subtopics.description: Solving equations where fractions and variables mix, e.g. x + 1/3 = 3x, x/4 + 2 = 5, (2x+1)/3 = x - 1. Fraction coefficients and fraction answers.

lesson.summary: An equation stays true as long as you do the exact same thing to both sides — like keeping a balance scale level.
lesson.example_text: x + 1/3 = 3x: subtract x from both sides to get 1/3 = 2x, then divide both sides by 2 to get x = 1/6.

subtopics.fallback_hint: Do the same thing to both sides of the equation to keep it balanced, then simplify.

constraints.denominators: unlike, one is a multiple of the other (e.g. 3 and 6)
coprime pairs allowed (e.g. 3 and 4), LCD required
constraints.multiplication: fraction x whole, fraction x fraction, small values

constraints.terms: up to 3, mixed operations with correct order of operations
constraints.cancelling: problems designed so cross-cancelling saves time

difficulty_ladder.label: Intro variables

constraints.equations: one-step and two-step, x on one side only

difficulty_ladder.example: x/4 = 3/8, find x   |   x + 1/3 = 5/6, find x

constraints.equations: x on both sides, fraction coefficients

styles: find a fraction between two fractions with smallest denominator
digit/unknown puzzles: a/b where conditions on a+b, a-b given

difficulty_ladder.label: Olympiad challenge

styles: work/rate problems (pipes, painters) requiring fraction reasoning
proof-flavored MCQ: 'which statement must be true'
competition-style: adapted from AMC 8 / Math Kangaroo difficulty

difficulty_ladder.example: A tank fills in 3 h with pipe A, 4 h with pipe B. Both open, tank already 1/6 full: how long to fill?

misconceptions.name: forgets to convert one fraction
misconceptions.description: Finds LCD but only converts one fraction: 2/3 + 1/6 -> 3/6
misconceptions.distractor_rule: convert only the first fraction to LCD, then add numerators

misconceptions.name: fails to simplify
misconceptions.description: Correct value but not in lowest terms: 3/8 + 1/8 -> 4/8

misconceptions.name: regrouping error
misconceptions.description: In mixed number subtraction, subtracts smaller from larger numerator regardless of order: 3 1/4 - 1 3/4 -> 2 2/4

misconceptions.name: finds common denominator to multiply
misconceptions.description: Applies addition procedure to multiplication: 2/3 x 1/4 -> converts to twelfths then multiplies numerators only

misconceptions.name: flips the wrong fraction
misconceptions.description: Inverts the dividend instead of the divisor: 3/4 / 1/2 -> 4/3 x 1/2 = 2/3

misconceptions.name: moves terms without inverse operation
misconceptions.description: x + 1/3 = 3x -> x = 3x + 1/3 (sign/direction error when moving terms)

misconceptions.name: divides only one side/term
misconceptions.description: 2x = 2/3 -> x = 2/3 - 2, or divides only one term of a sum by the coefficient

misconceptions.name: part-of-whole vs part-of-part
misconceptions.description: Takes fraction of the original quantity when the fraction applies to the remainder: 'ate 1/2, then 1/3 of the rest' -> computes 1/3 of the whole
misconceptions.distractor_rule: apply fraction to whole instead of remainder

speed_targets_seconds.comment: Target median time per problem, by level. Only tighten speed once accuracy >= 0.85 at that level.

mastery_rules.level_up_when: accuracy >= 0.85 over last 15 problems at current level AND median time <= speed target
mastery_rules.level_down_when: accuracy < 0.5 over last 10 problems at current level
mastery_rules.mastered_threshold: elo >= 1200 for the subtopic at grade-calibrated difficulty

generation_rules.distractor_policy: Each wrong option MUST map to a misconception id from this file. Include misconception_id in the stored option object.
generation_rules.position_policy: Shuffle answer positions uniformly; never let correct answer occupy the same position more than 3 times in a row within a session.
generation_rules.none_of_these: From level 6 up, 1 in 6 problems may use 'None of these' as an option (correct ~40% of the times it appears).
generation_rules.answer_storage: Store the correct answer as structured data: {type: 'fraction', numerator, denominator} or {type: 'expression', value}. Never store as display string only. This enables free-input mode later.
generation_rules.verification: Every generated problem must pass programmatic verification (math.js evaluation; for equations, substitute the solution back and check equality within 1e-9) before being saved. Discard and regenerate on failure.
generation_rules.language: Keep problem wording short and concrete. Names, objects, and contexts should rotate (pizza, ribbons, race laps, water tanks) and stay culturally neutral.
